statement: Fix 1 ≤ i ≤ n. Suppose that a field k, a central division algebra ∆0 over k, a formal space U, and a low-relation ideal Q ⊆ Symk U satisfy the induction conditions of Section 3, with the triangular identities already constructed for the rows d > i. Then there are a finitely generated extension F/k, a central division algebra ∆ over F, and an enlarged formal space and low-relation ideal over F satisfying the same conditions with the rows d ≥ i constructed. In particular, the enlarged formal space contains a form ti for which tai i = cifi + X l<i Bilfl + X d>i Cidtd (mod Qnew), ci ∈ F× . (8.4) All the enlarged formal forms evaluate to mutually commuting linear forms in ∆[x], and the new relation ideal is generated by linear forms and quadrics.
